title: Security Event Log
summary: Highlights risky account changes from other devices and groups a takeover-shaped burst, with a "This wasn't me" path the user can review.
description: Security activity log that highlights risky changes from other devices, groups a burst (new device, 2-step off, new recovery email) as a likely takeover, and offers "This wasn't me" with each remedy as an untickable checkbox. Times follow the account's zone.
catches: Risky changes from devices other than the current one
A burst of risky changes within windowMinutes, named as a likely takeover
Remedies listed before acting (sign out device, re-enable 2-step, restore recovery)
Required remedies that can't be unticked
Day grouping in the account's time zone
limits: Risk and grouping are heuristics over the events you pass
Location comes from IP and is approximate
Remedies run through your onConfirm; nothing is secured until the server does it
a11y: Remedy list is a group labelled by its title; Escape cancels
Remedy checkboxes have <label>s; "choose one" note is polite, errors are role=alert
Focus moves to the secure button on open and back to the row's report button on cancel
Times use <time> with a machine-readable dateTime
server: Run the remedies server-side (revoke sessions, restore factors) and require re-authentication or a recovery check before doing so.
stops: Account takeover buried in the activity log
